title: When quiet saves power
summary: Quiet buckets can skip work. Busy ones, and training, are different bills.

cards.text:
Three different savings get called “energy.”
Not switching. Not moving weights far away. Not doing a dense multiply you did not need.

A bucket that tips all the time saves none of the first.
Training on a graphics chip is a different bill entirely.

question.prompt: Which one is not, by itself, the chip savings?
choices: Training with a long diary on a graphics chip
Skipping work while a bucket is quiet
Keeping weights next to the buckets
question.why: Training cost and running cost are different.
question.simpler: Name which saving, and the baseline, before repeating a big ratio.

question.why: Too many things moved. The ratio is not about spikes alone.

recall.question: Does a bucket that tips constantly save energy just by being a spike?
